rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent long bar with a central void/cut and a small lifted or notched condition at one end, so it is not fragmented and it does respond to the provided neighborhood-living brief. The thin blue access edge is answered only modestly: the void is legible in plan and section, but the street response is more of a side seam than a strongly public threshold. The silhouette is coherent and not merely stair-stepped; it is a simple bar with a carved central slot and minor section shifts. Program fit is acceptable because neighborhood living can plausibly support an active ground edge, shared court/void, and calm upper mass, though the section is still fairly generic and slightly over-sealed for the brief. Overall this is a solid early massing with room to sharpen the access-facing public void and make the hierarchy more explicit.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Long, low mass with a carved central opening and a clear bridge/threshold condition can support neighborhood-scale publicness.
